title: Rerun what a change affects
prompt: Today's release changes the code of one task, `changed` in the starter. Its output and the outputs of the tasks below it are now out of date. Write `solve(shipments, shipment_events, deliveries)` so it returns those tasks only: each one's name in `task` and the number of rows its new output has in `rows`.
rules: A task is out of date when it is the changed task, or when it needs an out-of-date task, directly or through other tasks.
Tasks that aren't out of date keep yesterday's output: leave them out of the result. They may still have to run so the others get their inputs.
hints: Walk the tasks in `run_order(deps)`: a task is out of date when any task it needs is already on your list.
To get a task's new output you still need its inputs, so run every task in order and keep the outputs in a dict.
Count only the out-of-date outputs and build the result with `spark.createDataFrame(results, "task STRING, rows BIGINT")`.
explanation: Walking the run order once finds everything below the change: start the list with `known_events`, and add each later task that needs something already on the list. `delivered` needs `known_events` directly; `late_scans` and `in_flight` need it through `delivered`. `clean_events`, `unknown_events` and `late_deliveries` don't depend on it, so their outputs from yesterday are still right. Listing only the direct dependents misses `late_scans` and `in_flight`, which would keep stale counts. Walking `deps[name]` goes the other way, up to the tasks the changed one needs.
